newsitem.title: HUNGARY: World Bank extends $60 mln loan to Hungary MVM.
newsitem.headline: World Bank extends $60 mln loan to Hungary MVM.

text.p: The World Bank is extending Hungarian electricity supply company Magyar Villamos Muvek Rt (MVM) a $60 million loan for 15 years with a five-year grace period, Hungary's Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
The loan agreement was signed in Budapest today, the ministry said in a statement, while Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy signed a state guarantee on the loan.
MVM will have to start to repay the loan in September 2002 and payments are to be done half-yearly, "amid favourable interest conditions," it added.
MVM will use the loan to build two gas turbine reserve power plants of 120 megawatts each in Sajoszoged, north-east Hungary and Liter, central Hungary.
By the investment Hungary will fulfil its obligation taken when it joined the west European electricity network (UCPTE) in 1995.
Total costs of the investment are seen amounting to 16 billion forints, it said.
The loan might be drawn until June 30, 1999, while the investment is expected to be completed in 1998.
